searchText: Yes, this is the same thing we did for Glamsterdam. What was merged in glamsterdam before it was SFId? Can we add a discussion of this to acd? we always go CFI -> devnet -> SFI without a devnet we can't sfi it without the specs getting merged in we can't go to devnet 😄 so what are you proposing? glammy EIPs CFI date / merge date / SFI date the only exception for the rules are the headliner EIPs I guess. as headliners tend to get the SFI very early on to indicate "dedication" We don't need things in the spec before going to devnet, on the other direction we do need to implement the spec on our trunk branches to pass test vectors or skip possibly important tests (all tests that failed when the feature was added). This forces clients to implement in their trunk branches everything that goes on the specs repo regardless if it's SFId or not, which ultimately leads to whatever is on the spec to decide the scope of the fork instead of ACD. Once a feature lands in the repo the onus is on removing it rather than on sfiing it. If you need the features merged in the spec for devnet testing I'd say we do what we always did before which was the main branch plus feature branches that were being tested can clients not just skip "heze" tests? and just run those tests when they are ready on their trunks The point is that any Heze test that fails when you add the feature because of behavior test, is a test that needs to be skipped and thus the previous behavior is no longer tested Like barnabas said, you could simply disable heze tests OR you could say: * My gloas impl supports v1.7.0-beta.4 specs, run those tests for gloas. * My heze impl supports v1.7.0-beta.3 specs, run those tests for heze. But I imagine that would introduce even more complexity. So probably a bad idea. I think the issue potuz is having that he wants to make sure beta 4 passes for their heze tests too on trunk, but that would "force" them to implement the new EIPs. I think the process is working as intended tho. I think its fine to have failing tests for EIPs that you have not implemented yet? But also I do see how eip 8015 change just blows up everything else well, EIP 8015 itself is a simple one? and probably the most widely agreed upon single EIP on the CL side? yup agreed, so I would say to fix the runners just implement the EIP? The major issue I have is besides a technical point: the group of people that decide what gets merged in the spec repo is different than the group of people that decided what's SFId for a fork. And the influence of getting something merged makes it much more difficult to remove from the fork. Well, personally that's why I've viewed CFI as presumptive-SFI-by-default and why I find people's casual CFIs to be deeply disingenuous I think I wasn't clear what "failed test" means here. The fork is Heze, we have some tests. Code in our main branch passes it. A feature is added. That feature adds it's own tests. Skipping those tests is fine. However, when a feature is added, existing tests also fail without fixing them to account for the new behavior. If we skip those tests then we stop testing the original code we meant to test. Skipping these tests is not fine because yes the process leads this way like, no, most CFIs are not going to be undone, don't pretend CFI is not just trying something out But my angle is, take CFI more seriously then, not less Well that may be your interpretation but not what the process says. CFI is just considered for inclusion and many ssz EIPs have been CFId for long, and Verkle is the canonical example of a CFId EIP for multiple forks the process lies sorry, the process is "misleading" whether intentionally I can't say No, as mentioned above, disabling Heze is not what we want, we want to disable the features that aren't guaranteed to be in Heze, and that's impossible to do The cost of the alternate approach is what the EL side sees though -- a bunch of different devnet-test vectors, a bunch of different branches which all have to be maintained, etc. Different tradeoffs. Personally I like the CL approach -- try to be decisive about what's let in, and go with it I'm fine with this approach, but that approach to me means "we all decide on acd what's in as SFId and go with it". Not "Barnabas wants to test this, Justin merges it, and we all now either implement or skip previously passing tests" yeah I agree again this is exactly the process we did earlier, and it wasn’t raised as a potential issue before. So basically you are asking us to keep the consensus spec prs in prs and don’t merge anything into master till the eip is SFI-ed. And run all devnets with random branches of consensus specs ? I’m having a hard time understanding how that would work, as we couldn’t make alpha releases of the specs either, you would just have to have some random branches as the target for your tests I get what they're saying. For glamsterdam, we agreed to including those those in devnets very explicitly at the interop and in ACD calls. Whereas this time, we merged 8015 and 8365 into heze without that explicit approval. Yeah that's on me. We felt that these two EIPs were relatively simple, had strong support at ACD, that FOCIL was somewhat stable, and that we wanted to speed things up a bit this upgrade cycle. We did wait to merge 8198 because it was more controversial. From my understanding, the main problem here is the fact that it didn't go through public discussions. It was covered in ACDT yesterday but it was obviously not sufficient. Even that ACDT discussion was an after-the-fact fix. It's on me merging those two EIPs, I was the one who hit the merge buttons. I got a little too caught up in making a progress in two forks in parallel and let it get the better of me. Hindsight is 20/20, but urging people to move fast isn’t the answer. We should move fast without sacrificing rough consensus. Merging into master is fine. Eip7732 was in master for over a year. But it was only made glamsterdam after it was SFId Or rather Gloas
